core_claim: With well-defined rights and zero transaction costs, bargaining reaches the efficient outcome whatever the initial assignment of rights, so real transaction costs make rights and institutions decisive.
business_use: Designing emissions trading and resolving externality disputes

core_claim: Self-interested members of large groups free ride on shared goods, so groups organize only through selective incentives, coercion, or sanctions.
business_use: Funding industry consortia, trade associations, and open-source infrastructure

core_claim: With incomplete contracts, ownership confers residual control rights that shape ex post bargaining power and ex ante investment, so assets should be owned by the party whose investment matters most.
business_use: Make-or-buy decisions and allocating ownership in alliances and joint ventures

core_claim: Because search is costly, buyers and workers stop before finding the best offer, so price dispersion and coexisting unemployment and vacancies are equilibrium outcomes.
business_use: Pricing transparency strategy and reducing time-to-hire

core_claim: Firms pay above market-clearing wages because higher pay raises effort, deters shirking, and reduces turnover, leaving involuntary unemployment in equilibrium.
business_use: Setting wage premiums to cut turnover and raise productivity

core_claim: When a product's value rises with its number of users, expectations become self-fulfilling and markets can tip to one standard and lock in.
business_use: Standards battles, launch pricing, and compatibility decisions

core_claim: Platforms linking two groups with cross-side network effects choose a price structure that often subsidizes one side and earns margin on the other.
business_use: Platform pricing for payment cards, app stores, and ride-hailing

core_claim: Auction rules and information determine bidding, revenue, and efficiency, and in common-value settings naive winners overpay (the winner's curse).
business_use: Designing procurement, advertising, and spectrum auctions

core_claim: Formal rules and informal constraints shape transaction costs and incentives and thereby explain long-run differences in economic performance.
business_use: Assessing institutional environments for market entry and governance choice

core_claim: Many people care about others' payoffs and fairness and will pay to punish unfair treatment, which constrains prices, wages, and contracts.
business_use: Communicating price increases and avoiding price-gouging backlash
